ceiling_statement: Maximum achievable legal-reasoning correctness under H1-H8 is: provable soundness AND completeness of every emitted legal conclusion with respect to the unique grounded (well-founded) extension of an explicitly committed, finite, defeasible rulebase, where (a) every conclusion carries a machine-checkable derivation certificate re-verifiable offline (H5/H8), (b) defeater sensitivity is total over the committed rulebase (every admitted defeater that attacks a derivation is guaranteed to defeat or be defeated in the labelling, including cyclic attack structures, which terminate with label :out/:undefined), and (c) every question whose answer depends on unformalized or interpretively contested source text returns typed UNKNOWN (H2). No feasible system can additionally guarantee correctness of the natural-language-to-rule formalization step itself, nor resolve genuinely contested interpretation.
derivation: Three independent limits pin this ceiling. (1) Computability: full first-order defeasible logic is undecidable, and credulous acceptance under preferred/stable argumentation semantics is NP-hard and non-unique, violating H5 determinism; the grounded/well-founded semantics is the unique maximal semantics that is simultaneously deterministic (single minimal complete extension), polynomial-time computable (alternating-fixpoint on a finite lattice, hence provably terminating), and certificate-carrying (each label has a finite well-founded derivation tree). Any 'stronger' semantics either loses uniqueness (breaks H5 replay) or decidability (breaks H3 fail-closed termination). (2) Information theory: the bytes of a statute underdetermine its legal meaning (open texture; contested interpretation is not a computable function of the committed text), so correctness 'about the law itself' is not machine-decidable by ANY system; the supremum is correctness relative to a committed formal rulebase plus honest UNKNOWN at the formalization boundary. (3) H1 closes the only escape hatch: a statistical model cannot be trusted to certify the NL-to-formal mapping, so that mapping enters only as attested, admitted input whose certificate records who/what asserted it — never as trusted inference. Therefore sound+complete grounded-extension computation with derivation certificates plus typed UNKNOWN at the interpretation boundary is the ceiling; exceeding it requires deciding an undecidable or non-encoded question.
relativity_note: Relative to the grounded (well-founded) semantics of finite defeasible rule systems — Dung's grounded extension, equivalently the well-founded model of the corresponding logic program (Van Gelder-Ross-Schlipf). Correctness claims are meaningful only against this committed formal semantics of the admitted rulebase, never against 'the law' as natural-language text.
attainment_mechanism: Extend the existing JTMS engine behind systems/orchestrator-cli/inference-gate.lisp (which already implements well-founded defeaters, repealed-node non-propagation, cyclic-justification termination, and :derived proof structures over a real 3000-event chain) into a certified alternating-fixpoint labeller in pure SBCL: monotone operator on the finite node lattice, iterated to fixpoint (termination = lattice finiteness, provable by induction), each label emitting an S-expression derivation tree; a separate independent checker package (no shared state with the producer, per H8 recompute-and-compare, same pattern as authority-v2/proofs/verify-proof-manifest.py) re-validates every derivation offline. Deontic premises enter only through the frozen adversarial suite discipline of systems/orchestrator-cli/deontic-gate.lisp + source/legal-extraction-verify.lisp, admitted as attested facts under the conjuncts of authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp; interpretation-dependent queries return the typed UNKNOWN already institutionalized by the honest-ceiling judge pattern. Deterministic conflict cores source/legal-conflict-resolution.lisp and source/legal-counterfactual.lisp supply lex-superior/posterior/specialis priorities as explicit committed rules, not heuristics. All of this is plain Common Lisp + SHA-256 commitments — buildable today.
b0_gap: B0 map (AX-01 row + section 3): the JTMS is PROOF_CARRYING only on frozen example suites — 'example-driven, not proven for all graphs'; the deontic classifier is a linguistic heuristic (~81.5-91.5%), not a formally specified deontic grammar with a soundness proof; the jurisprudence judge measures co-citation frequency, not correctness; systems/orchestrator-epistemic/meta-ontology.lisp honestly declares conflict resolution ABSENT by design (slw:doesNotResolveConflicts true, slw:doesNotSelectInterpretation true, verified at lines 122-168); admission theorems T1-T9 in authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp are 0/17 proved; and the constitutional gate fails open on predicate error. The gap is the distance from 'passes fixed adversarial cases' to 'sound and complete for ALL finite rulebases, machine-checked'.
lean_obligation: Given a finite attack/support graph G = (N, just : N -> List (List N × List N)) (justifications with in-lists and out-lists), define the alternating-fixpoint operator Φ on labellings L : N -> {in, out, undefined}. Prove: (T1) Φ has a unique least fixpoint wf(G) and the implemented iteration computes it in ≤ |N| rounds (termination + uniqueness, hence deterministic replay); (T2) soundness — every node labelled `in` by the implementation possesses a finite well-founded derivation tree all of whose defeaters are labelled `out`; (T3) completeness — every node `in` the well-founded model is labelled `in`; (T4) defeater sensitivity — adding any admitted defeater d attacking node n either flips n to out/undefined or yields a certificate that d is itself out; (T5) UNKNOWN monotonicity — `undefined` never satisfies the acceptance predicate (no upgrade to pass). Each theorem is a statement about total functions on finite structures, directly formalizable in Lean 4 (Fintype N, WellFoundedRecursion).
